body.p: REMARKS
This communication is responsive to the Office Action dated October 30, 2023 and is

accompanied with an RCE. Applicant has amended claims 1, 11, 21, and 22. Claims 1 - 5, 8 - 15, and 18 - 22 remain pending upon entry of this Amendment. Applicant notes that claims 16 and 17 were canceled in the amendment filed December 19, 2023, which was entered.
Claim Interpretation Under 35 U.S.C. 4 112

In the Office Action, the Examiner noted that 35 U.S.C. § 112 (f) has not been invoked when interpreting claims 21 because "means for sensing," "means for determining," and means for selecting" "refers to one or more processors." Applicant acknowledges the Examiner's interpretation under 35 U.S.C. § 112 (f).

In the Office Action, the Examiner rejected claims 1-5 and 8-22 under 35 U.S.C. § 112, first paragraph, asserting that claims 1-5 and 8-22 are not supported by Applicant's specification. The Examiner asserted that "the independent claims, the specification fails to provide adequate written description for a method or a system comprising one or more processors configured to select a first frequency band of interest and a second frequency band of interest, and one or more processors configured to control therapy delivery by a medical device based on determined first and second biomarkers."2
As discussed in the Amendment in Response to Office Action filed August 14, 2023,

Applicant disagrees. As noted previously, Applicant's specification explicitly states that that the processing circuitry may determine, "one or more frequency bands of interest using any suitable technique."3 One of ordinary skill in the art would not have interpreted determining one or more frequency bands of interest as ONLY "select a first frequency band of interest," as characterized by the Examiner.
Similarly, Applicant's specification explicitly states that the "pattern of the power
distribution over one or more frequency sub-bands indicative of a particular patient state can be

within the same frequency band or over one or more frequency bands,"4 and paragraph [0040] also discloses "characteristics observed in the distribution of the signal strength over one or more frequency sub-bands of a frequency band of interest." Applicant's specification further states, "sensing module 66 includes a frequency selective sensing circuit that extracts the energy level within one or more selected frequency bands and sub-bands of a sensed patient parameter signal, which may be, for example, a bioelectrical brain signal."5 In paragraph [0097], Applicant's specification states that "Applicant's specification also describes, "the one or more frequency band characteristics meet a particular set of criteria (e.g., a particular spectral pattern) associated with the biomarker."6 From at least these portions Applicant's specification, along with Applicant's FIG. 9 as discussed in the previous response, Applicant's originally filed patent application clearly describes "the claimed invention in sufficient detail that one skilled in the art can reasonably conclude that the inventor had possession of the claimed invention."?

Specifically, from at least the excerpts from Applicant's written description above, one or ordinary skill in the art would have understood that Applicant's specification reciting "one or more frequency bands of interest" is evidence that the inventors had, at the time of filing, possession of "selecting a first frequency band of interest" and "selecting a second frequency band of interest," in addition to sub-bands within each frequency band, as recited by claim 1. Moreover, though not explicitly claimed, one of ordinary skill in the art would have understood that selecting one or more frequency bands of interest further includes selecting a third frequency band of interest, selecting a fourth frequency band of interest, selecting a fifth frequency band interest and so on.

Accordingly, for at least the reasons discussed above, Applicant amended independent claims are supported by Applicant's specification, in accordance with 35 U.S.C. § 112(a). Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of all rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a).

For at least these reasons, Applicant's current patent application is an application which is also disclosed in the prior application (the parent or original nonprovisional application or provisional application). The disclosure of the invention in the parent application and in the

In the Office Action, the Examiner rejected claims 1-5 and 8-22 under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) as allegedly being unpatentable over U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2009/0082691 by Denison et al. (hereinafter, "Denison") in view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2007/0197930 by Sarkela (hereinafter, "Sarkela") as evidenced by U.S. Patent No. 5,601,090 by Musha (hereinafter, "Musha"), further in view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2008/0228100 by Navakatikyan (hereinafter, "Navakatikyan").
Without conceding the merits of the rejection, Applicant has amended the claims to

expeditated prosecution towards allowance. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejections to the extent the rejections are applicable to the amended claims. The applied references, alone or in any combination, do not disclose or suggest the subject matter defined by Applicant's claims, and there would have been no apparent reason that would have caused one of ordinary skill in the art to modify the applied references to arrive at the claimed subject matter.
The Examiner cited to Navakatikyan to correct an admitted deficiency of Denison in

view of Sarkela to disclose or suggest "one or more of a peak width less than or equal to a first threshold value or a peak width greater than or equal to a second threshold value" as recited by Applicant's claim 1, for example. The Examiner characterized Navakatikyan as "identifying a biomarker comprising a unimodal peak or a bimodal peak."8 Contrary to the Examiner's characterization, Navakatikyan instead describes calculations to determine, "the amplitude of a peak and a trough in each data group,"9 which includes determining "the time interval between the peak and/or the trough."10 Navakatikyan does not describe identifying a biomarker. Further, Navakatikyan does not describe, and Applicant's claim 1 does not recite, "identifying whether a variability in the amplitude (unimodal peak) of one or more frequency sub-bands exhibits a relatively high or low level of activity."11

The Examiner further asserted that a unimodal or a bimodal peak "inherently has a peak width greater than a threshold value (the threshold value being zero)."12 The Examiner's interpretation of the threshold being zero is not reasonable because then there is no peak. In other words, the one or more processors would be unable to even determine a peak width if there is no peak. The Examiner's interpretation of a threshold being zero so that there is no peak to even have a peak width, removes this claim term from the claim and is thus not a reasonable interpretation.

Nonetheless, Applicant has amended claim 1 to recites, inter alia, "wherein the first predetermined characteristic of the first distribution comprises a first peak width less than or equal to a first non-zero threshold value or greater than or equal to a second non-zero threshold value" and "wherein the second predetermined characteristic of the second distribution comprises a second peak width less than or equal to a third non-zero threshold value or greater than or equal to a fourth non-zero threshold value." Since the threshold value is now a non-zero threshold value, even the Examiner's interpretation of Navakatikyan does not disclose this subject matter of amended claim 1.

For at least these reasons, the cited references alone or in any reasonable combination, do not disclose or suggest the subject matter defined by Applicant's claim 1, and there would have been no apparent reason that would have caused one of ordinary skill in the art to modify the applied references to arrive at the claimed subject matter. Amended independent claims 11, 21, and 22 include subject similar to that recited by claim 1 and arguments with regard to claim 1 apply equally to independent claims 11, 21, and 22.

For at least the reasons discussed above, amended independent claims 1, 11, 21, and 22 are patentable over the cited references. The dependent claims incorporate the requirements of the respective independent claims.13 Accordingly, the dependent claims are likewise patentable.
For at least these reasons, Applicant's amended claims 1 - 5, 8 - 15, and 18 - 22 are
patentable under 35 U.S.C. § 103. Applicant therefore respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of all rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 103.

CONCLUSION
All claims in this application are in condition for allowance. Applicant does not

acquiesce as to any assertion in the Office Action with respect to the cited art or to Applicant's claims. Applicant's silence with respect to any assertion in the Office Action should not be interpreted as Applicant's acquiescence thereto. Applicant reserves the right to comment further with respect to the applied references and any pending claim in a future Amendment, Response, or on appeal. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and prompt allowance of all pending claims.

Applicant does not concede that the subject matter encompassed by the claims prior to this Response is unpatentable over the art cited by the Office Action. While several distinctions have been noted over the art of record, Applicant notes that there may be several other limitations that are neither taught nor suggested by the art of record. Applicant expressly reserves all rights and arguments with respect to distinctions not explicitly noted herein. In addition, to the extent that amendments included herein constitute a narrowing of the claims, such narrowing of the claims should not be construed as an admission as to the merits of the prior rejections. Indeed, Applicant traverses the rejections and preserves all rights and arguments. To the extent that any particular statement or argument by the Office in the pending Office Action has not been explicitly addressed herein, the same should not be construed as an acquiescence or admission by the Applicant that such statements or arguments by the Office are accurate and proper.
